result.summary: Out of 40 ZTARE cycles, the vast majority (33) are straightforwardly not theory-building: they are verification-iteration moves — decomposing obligations, installing gate apparatus, collapsing null results, or refining algorithmic search strategies within a fixed adversarial-verification substrate. Only 7 cycles meet at least the medium-confidence threshold for a genuine theory-building operation, and even those are marginal: C11 and C22 (ns) codify tacit practices into formal apparatus (tb_06); C19 (ns) targets a structural barrier via a Killing-mode falsifier (tb_NEW_POLYA); C20 (ns) installs a constraint list that forces unique form (tb_04); C23 (aqual) codifies an implicit provenance audit (tb_06); C39 and C40 (neural) add constraint gates and paired-primitive specifications (tb_04, tb_06 respectively). The ns substrate shows the highest density of borderline theory-building moves, likely because it is constructing a Lean proof architecture where formalizing implicit proof-routing practices is structurally necessary; the aqual and neural substrates are predominantly engaged in epistemic-downgrade and search-procedure iteration with almost no theory-building signal.
